comment: The draft provides useful lifecycle governance for semantic artefacts and recommends continuing national conformance monitoring. However, it does not yet make explicit how a product-level certification result remains interpretable as the normative baseline evolves. Without an explicit binding to the versions tested, a product may remain labelled “certified” even after relevant profiles, terminology resources, test suites or product releases have materially changed.

public.text: The draft provides useful lifecycle governance for semantic artefacts and recommends continuing national conformance monitoring. However, it does not yet make explicit how a product-level certification result remains interpretable as the normative baseline evolves. Without an explicit binding to the versions tested, a product may remain labelled “certified” even after relevant profiles, terminology resources, test suites or product releases have materially changed.
public.suggestedRevision:
Make each conformance statement or certificate explicitly version-scoped. At minimum, record the tested actor role(s), profile or implementation-guide version, relevant logical-model and terminology/value-set versions, test-suite version and product release. Define expiry or reassessment triggers for material specification or product changes, together with a transition policy for overlapping versions and risk-based post-deployment surveillance. This would complement, rather than duplicate, the document’s existing artefact-lifecycle governance

This is a distinct but related concern to the assurance operating model proposed in comment 5: this comment addresses what a conformance statement should record, while comment 5 addresses who should be authorised to issue it.
